summary: Publish Go binaries for multiple operating systems from version tags, with archives, checksums, changelogs and optional Homebrew distribution.
description: Turn version tags into Go release archives with matching binary version metadata, checksums and a commit-based changelog. A local snapshot build exercises release packaging without publishing. The default targets include Linux, macOS and Windows on Intel and ARM; optional Homebrew publishing needs its own tap and credentials. This fragment extends a Go binary project rather than providing installer or self-update behavior.
seoDescription: GoReleaser configuration for tagged Go releases, target archives, checksums, version metadata, local snapshots and optional Homebrew publishing.

projectExamples.title: Downloadable operator utility
projectExamples.description: Distribute a custom Go command-line tool as release archives for the configured targets. Implement its operator commands in the base stack.

projectExamples.title: Homebrew-installed developer tool
projectExamples.description: Enable the optional Homebrew publisher for a Go utility. Supply the tap repository and token, then test the chosen publishing configuration.

plain.whatItIs: Turns version labels pushed to Git into downloadable builds of a Go command-line program for Windows, macOS and Linux, with checksums.
goodAt: Building one program for Windows, macOS and Linux on Intel and ARM chips
Publishing release files with checksum files and a changelog written from commit messages
notGoodAt: Programs built with Bun, a JavaScript runtime; use the Bun release add-on for those.

requests: publish downloadable builds of my Go tool whenever I push a version tag

preview release artifacts locally before making them public
